body.statement: Import the lossless exact labelled eight-type orbit-game reduction established in the accepted repository parent \(\texttt{exp\_multiarm\_secondorder\_minimax\_frontier}\). For every \(n\), common permutation symmetrization identifies \[\rho_n^{\mathrm{all}}=G_n^{\mathrm{all}},\qquad \rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)=G_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q).\] Its exact likelihood is \(P_m(x\mid r)\), and its attained finite primal and dual games retain zero arm counts and zero-likelihood observation cells.
body.justification: This imported proposition is infrastructure only: it fixes the exact labelled finite experiment on which the new asymptotic claims are built.
body.gap: No novelty is claimed for the orbit equality; the accepted repository parent supplies it, while the unresolved step is its uniform second-order analysis at the singular face/corner fiber.
body.consumer: The imported finite experiment is the common starting point for the Airy constant, the singular bridge, and the allocation-frontier claims.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathfrak S_n\) act simultaneously on unit labels in schedules, assignments, and observed data.  Fix any schedule-independent pair \((\mathcal D,\widehat\tau)\).  Draw \(\sigma\) uniformly from \(\mathfrak S_n\), apply \((\mathcal D,\widehat\tau)\) after relabelling by \(\sigma\), and undo the relabelling in the reported data.  For every schedule \(z\), the risk of this randomized symmetrization is the average of the original risks over \(\{\sigma z:\sigma\in\mathfrak S_n\}\), and hence is at most \(\max_{z'}R_n(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau;z')\).  Conditional averaging of the reported action given the observed data cannot increase squared loss, by
\[
  \mathbb E\{D-\tau\}^2
  =\{\mathbb E(D\mid O)-\tau\}^2+\operatorname{Var}(D\mid O).
\]
Thus a deterministic invariant rule is sufficient.

An invariant assignment law is constant on each orbit of \(\mathcal A^n\).  Such an orbit is indexed by \(r\), has \(n!/\prod_a r_a!\) elements, and the invariant law is therefore uniquely a mixture \(\pi\) of the uniform laws on these orbits.  An observed binary labelled array has orbit invariant \((r,x)\), so an invariant deterministic action is exactly a function \(\delta(r,x)\).  Similarly, two complete schedules are in the same orbit exactly when their eight response-type counts \(m\) agree; hence maximization over schedules becomes maximization over \(\mathcal M_n\).

Fix \(m,r,x\).  A latent table \(h\in\mathcal H(m,r,x)\) can be realized by
\[
  \prod_{t\in\mathcal T}\frac{m_t!}{\prod_{a\in\mathcal A}h_{t,a}!}
\]
labelled assignments.  Dividing the sum of these counts by the orbit size \(n!/\prod_a r_a!\) gives
\[
 P_m(x\mid r)
 =\frac{\prod_a r_a!}{n!}
   \sum_{h\in\mathcal H(m,r,x)}
   \prod_{t\in\mathcal T}\frac{m_t!}{\prod_a h_{t,a}!}.
\]
Substitution in the invariant risk gives exactly \(G_n^{\mathrm{all}}\).  Under \(\mathcal D_q\), exchangeability gives
\[
 \pi_r=\frac{n!}{\prod_a r_a!}\prod_aq_a^{r_a},
\]
which gives \(G_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)\).  All spaces are finite and the action interval is compact, so the minima are attained.  No step removes an orbit with \(r_a=0\); if \(P_m(x\mid r)=0\), its term is simply zero and its primal constraint remains present.  This proves both displayed equalities and the asserted support conventions.
